newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Robinson sees higher second half profit.
newsitem.headline: Robinson sees higher second half profit.

text.p: Robinson & Co Ltd, one of Singapore's oldest department stores groups, said on Wednesday it expects profits in the second half of its fiscal year to be higher than the first half, company officials said on Wednesday.
"In terms of profits, second half should be bigger than in the first half," chief executive officer Peter Husum said at a meeting with media and investment analysts.
The retailer reported on February 25 a 20.9 percent gain in first half profit to Singapore $13.68 million while turnover rose 12.3 percent to S$119.43 million.
The performance was a pleasant surprise for the group, which had said last year it expected flat earnings.

"We weren't too optimistic about (Singapore's) economy," said chairman Michael Wong. "So we took the view results would be flat but it turned out better than expected with a pick-up in October to December."
Husum said the group's expansions and new shopping outlets in Singapore last year are already contributing positively to turnover and earnings.
Robinson will be opening an 800 sq ft "Sports Girl" outlet in Singapore in April. It is also planning to open a 30,000 sq ft "Marks & Spencer" outlet in Kuala Lumpur in late 1997 or beginning 1998.
Regional expansion plans, apart from in Malaysia, are unlikely, according to Wong.
"Regionally, the markets are protected. If you go into countries like Thailand and Indonesia, you are expected to find a local partner. We have to weigh the returns," Wong said.
The group had a total of 225,800 sq ft of retail space in Singapore and Malaysia as of December 1, 1996.
